 'Ferris Bueller' Sequel Ad Reunites Jennifer Grey, Charlie Sheen
 by Les Luchter 
 , 
 Yesterday
 Caregiving provider Home Instead’s new 40 th -anniversary sequel to “Ferris Bueller’s Day Off” features Ferris’ sister Jeanie -- reprised by Jennifer
Grey -- who’s forced to play caregiver for Mom and Dad as her brother is again taking the day off. While searching for Ferris, Jeanie consults with Garth (a returning Charlie Sheen), who again
tells her to stop worrying about her brother and start worrying about herself -- but this time suggests she call Home Instead.
 Cindy Pickett as Ferris’ mom also returns. But not Ferris
himself: Matthew Broderick. But that’s just fine since the Jeanie character is “aligned with the target audience we’re so often speaking to: the adult daughter, who ends up bearing a
lot of the caregiving load at the holidays,” Kim Atkinson, Home Instead’s chief brand and communications officer, tells Marketing Daily. 
 advertisement
 advertisement
 Elaborating on the brand’s
typical customers, she points to “Gen X’ers and elder millennials who are caring for their aging parents or making decisions with their siblings on how to get care…This customer
also often has her own children living at home, so they’re caring for multi-generational families.’”
 The campaign follows last year’s 35 th -anniversary sequel to “Home Alone,” in which a now-middle-aged Kevin, reprised by
 Macaulay  Culkin, played caregiver to his aging mom.  That campaign also had one significant missing character from its original film -- Kevin’s mom -- which
took on added poignance when Catherine O’Hara, who played the role in the original, died just a couple of weeks after the commercial’s last airing on Golden Globes Sunday last January.
 This year’s output, with creative from Omnicom’s BBDO Chicago and media buying by Atlanta’s Fitzco, is also scheduled to run through the Golden Globes on Jan. 10. That’s
because “a lot of people are thinking about movies” at that time, Atkinson explains.
 The campaign --  which includes :30 , :15 and :06 cutdowns in addition to the hero :60 -- will run on broadcast, connected
TV, social and programmatic display.
 “Families are together over the holidays,” Atkinson says in explaining the timing of Home Instead’s now-annual movie-themed
campaigns.
 The brand’s linear TV strategy is largely focused on “moments where people are thinking about the holidays and gathering to watch content together,” she relates.
This includes “some college football placements,” NBC’s “Saturday Night Live” Thanksgiving special (which usually runs in prime time on Thanksgiving Eve) and, most
prominently “movie marathons on various channels.”
 Watching holiday movies  is the top activity families do together during the holiday season,  Atkinson explains, and
the Home Instead ads provide an “unexpected connection with nostalgic times when they were children…to characters that feel familiar, but imagining what it would be like if those
characters grew up and suddenly had a very different relationship to their families.” 
 The campaign buy also includes social posts by both Grey and Sheen; digital billboards in
Chicago, where the original movie was filmed; and a “Nominate a Jeanie” giveaway, in which people are invited to “submit a story about someone they know who is a ‘Jeanie’
(female or male) and could use a little bit of help around the holidays,” Atkinson says. The winner will receive an unspecified level of support from Home Instead.
 Home Instead’s
total holiday campaign media investment is up over last year, Atkinson says, because the brand is now offering a toolkit of assets to its 600+ franchisees, allowing them to get involved in their local
areas.  This can include such activities as social sharing or hosting branded nostalgia-themed trivia nights which could involve hospitals and other partners “who they so often work
with,” she says.
 “What we’re trying to communicate with these campaigns is that the aging journey is not an easy one,” Atkinson notes. “There are hard
conversations that families have to have. And so many people don’t even know that getting help from an in-home caregiver is an option.”
 Last year’s campaign generated 1.6
billion earned media impressions (DeVries is the agency behind that) and a 6.38x ROI, Atkinson notes, and that this year, “we hope to drive even more ongoing cultural conversation about the
sandwich generation: there’s a better way to think about aging and the care that aging adults get.”
 As for the 2027 holiday season, Atkinson hints that she and her team are already
looking at what movie they could revisit. “We want to be the brand that comes up with conversation that nobody is expecting, but really touches people in a meaningful way,” she
declares.
